one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes on Easter Sunday with sad and good news about the Manila Cathedral. The sad news: Archbishop Tagle directed its closure upon the Manila Cathedral-Basilica Foundation's recommendation after a structural engineering team led by Dr. Angel Lazaro III, conducting extensive tests including 30-meter bore holes, determined that soil liquefaction could occur in a major earthquake and endanger the church -- affecting 200 couples scheduled to marry there and ending the annual December pipe organ concerts. Cardinal Rosales had already suspected deterioration, arranging the removal of the cathedral's seven big bells (17 tons) from the belfry and installing computerized Holland carillon bells donated by Alberto and Sylvia Lina -- which also now must be brought down. The good news: at a recent private dinner among Archbishop Tagle, Amb. de Villa, CJ, and San Miguel Corp. president Ramon Ang, Ang 'graciously agreed to contribute P50 million to lead in saving this veritable center of Catholic worship.' The MCBF -- with the Archbishop as ex-officio chair, Amb. de Villa as vice chair, CJ Panganiban as president, and Marixi Prieto as vice president -- is now confident the cathedral can reopen within a year. CJ traces the cathedral's history from its 1581 original construction through World War II devastation and the 1958 reconstruction by Archbishop Rufino J. Santos (the first Filipino cardinal) to its elevation as a basilica by Pope John Paul II, describing it as 'the bulwark of Filipino Catholicism and an enduring witness to the strength and depth of our people's fidelity to our Lord Jesus Christ.'
